topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes for the hallmarks of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer frames the lecture by outlining learning outcomes, tumor progression models, and the framework of cancer hallmarks.

topics.label: Growth signal autonomy and pathway deregulation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how oncogenic mutations in receptor tyrosine kinase, Wnt, and downstream signaling cascades drive growth signal independence and resistance to growth inhibition.

topics.label: Block to terminal differentiation in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer cells evade terminal differentiation and maintain a proliferative progenitor state in hematologic malignancies and intestinal epithelium.

topics.label: Resistance to apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores how cancer cells evade programmed cell death through mutations in p53 and deregulation of Bcl-2 family proteins.

topics.label: Replicative immortality, senescence, and p53 stress responses
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how telomere shortening triggers senescence and how cancer cells bypass replicative limits and p53-mediated stress checkpoints to achieve immortalization.

topics.label: Cancer metabolic rewiring and oncometabolites
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce complex cancer hallmarks and explain metabolic reprogramming in tumors, including aerobic glycolysis, tissue-of-origin metabolic profiles, and oncometabolite-driven epigenetic alterations.

topics.label: Tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the angiogenic switch, the balance of regulatory factors, and the requirement of new blood vessel formation for tumor growth.

topics.label: Mechanisms, monitoring, and genetics of tumor metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the metastatic cascade, the use of circulating tumor cells as liquid biopsies, metastatic inefficiency, and the genomic alterations associated with metastatic dissemination.

topics.label: Summary and conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the lecture by summarizing how cancer hallmarks operate together and offering closing remarks.
